report.answer_text:
In the U.S., 40 hours a week is a common full-time schedule, but it’s not a legal minimum. The Fair Labor Standards Act doesn’t define full-time employment, so employers generally set their own cutoff. (dol.gov)
For health coverage under the Affordable Care Act’s employer rules, full-time means averaging at least 30 hours of service per week, or 130 hours per month. (irs.gov)
If you’re asking about your own job, check your employee handbook or ask HR what cutoff applies to your job status and the specific benefit you’re asking about.
